description: Whether two accounts on one network reach the same people: reads the commenters under each one's recent posts and returns both sets' sizes, the commenters who appear under both, and the overlap in each direction (the share of A's commenters also under B is a different number from the share of B's also under A). It measures engaged commenters on a few posts, not followers. Pass two handles, or one plus your own. Costs 4 nooticr credits for the two post lists plus 2 per post opened — 16 credits at the default of 3 posts each; postsPerCreator is the price. Use when deciding between one or two finalists of a collaboration shortlist, before approaching them.

commentsPerPost.description: Comments to read per post (default 50, max 50).

platform.description: Platform. Defaults to tiktok, so SET IT whenever the user named a network — otherwise a question about X, LinkedIn or Reddit is silently answered with TikTok data, and an empty result looks like the account does not exist. Accepts what get_user_posts does: tiktok, instagram, youtube, douyin, xiaohongshu, twitter, bilibili, linkedin, reddit, weibo.

postsPerCreator.description: Recent posts to open per account (default 3, max 8). Each one is a comment fetch, so this is the price.

usernames.description: The two handles to compare, with or without @, on the same network.

name: measure_audience_overlap

evidenceFrom.description: The cheap calls this was assembled from.

frameIndex.description: Where each returned frame sits in the video.

guidance.description: What to do with this payload, in prose. Read it: it is the instruction, not a summary.

measures.description: Always "engaged_commenters": commenters on a few recent posts, not followers.

mode.description: Always "evidence": this payload is material you have still to read.

overlap.description: Both directions: the share of `from`'s commenters who also commented under `to`.

shared.description: Commenters found under both accounts, most active first.

thinSample.description: True when either side has too few commenters for the share to mean much.

title: Measure Audience Overlap
